source.title: Dead-Direction Signatures: A Cheap Spectral Reading of Singular Complexity
source.authors: Tejas Pradeep Shirodkar; P. J. Narayanan

page_placements.theme: Complexity measures have distinct training trajectories

record.tranche_reason: The study reports grokking-related observations, but its experiments evaluate spectral measures of singular geometry, not the claim versions' specified training-versus-test accuracy delay, circuit mechanism, or causes of that delay.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-accuracy-defined grokking timings and compares validation accuracy with geometric observables. It does not report the timing of training-accuracy saturation relative to test accuracy, or a training-set-size sweep of the delay. Its DDS trajectory results are related to grokking but do not test the specified versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses two standard grokking benchmarks (Nanda modular addition, Barak sparse parity) as testbeds for its own spectral observables (DDS). Its results concern how σmin, u⊤Gu, λmin(G) and LLC behave across val_acc-anchored phases. It never measures training-accuracy saturation against test accuracy, generalizing or memorizing circuits, or any cause of the delay. It relies on grokking as a tool rather than testing it, so T4 fits better than the reader's T6/discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that DDS gives cheap closed-form spectral readings of dead directions, complementary to calibrated LLC. DDS tracks closed-form RLCT as a sanity gate, and the log det+ slope counts rank-deficit. On grokking benchmarks, DDS observables drop sharply across phases while LLC plateaus. The algorithmic (val_acc) transition is synchronous with the geometric one on Nanda AdamW+CE but precedes it on Barak SGD+MSE. They make no claim about the grokking phenomenon itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation and Fisher-Gram spectral measurements to track singular geometry; it does not reproduce the original grokking training-accuracy/test-accuracy analysis or the mechanistic-interpretability method.
record.method_sensitivity: The relationship between validation accuracy and geometric observables differs by setting: it is synchronous on Nanda with AdamW+CE and separated by thousands of steps on Barak with SGD+MSE. DDS numerical readings also depend on precision and regularization choices, but those are measurement-protocol effects, not tests of V7's proposed cause of grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: On Nanda (AdamW+CE), val_acc and u⊤Gu at the dead direction change synchronously at grokking. On Barak (SGD+MSE), the geometric approach to the singular minimum lags val_acc by thousands of steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric (Fisher/activation) collapse toward a singular minimum may coincide with or lag the grokking accuracy transition, depending on the optimizer and loss.

fits_no_version.finding: LLC rises about 4× pre-grok and then plateaus through the at-grok and cleanup phases (Table 2/3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The local learning coefficient changes mainly before the grokking transition and is flat afterwards in these settings.

record.code_released: The paper says the code will be released publicly on GitHub; in the interim it is available from the authors on request. No URL stated.
record.problems: The grokking timing summaries do not give training-accuracy saturation times or quantify test accuracy as a function of training time and training-set size. Several trajectory comparisons concern geometric observables rather than the claim's accuracy relationship.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were omitted. DDS spectral trajectories, sharpness ratios, and other singular-geometry results were left out because they do not measure the claim versions' specified behaviors.

untested.parts: Train-accuracy saturation relative to the test-accuracy jump. A grok-step-vs-ntrain sweep exists for Barak but is val_acc timing only, without the delay.
No circuit identification, no Fourier mechanism, no memorization-removal measure. DDS observables are not presented as progress measures anticipating the jump.
No non-algorithmic data and no init-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning grokking.
Weight decay is fixed per setup. There is no critical dataset size and no ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
Numerical precision (fp32 vs fp64, Tikhonov) affects only the DDS measurements, not whether grokking occurs.

missing.what: Barak grok step at ntrain = 1000, 5000 and 25000: about 6000, 1250–1300 and 1400–1600 steps respectively. These are val_acc-defined, with no train-accuracy saturation reported. They could matter to readers comparing data-size effects on grokking time, but cannot establish a delay.

record.verdict_notes: Grokking benchmarks serve only as testbeds for DDS, so no verdicts are given. A figure shows train accuracy, but no saturation timing is reported numerically. The Barak setup gives inconsistent step counts (30k vs 240k).

versions.untested_parts: The study reports grokking timings, but not whether training accuracy saturated while test accuracy remained at chance, the subsequent test-accuracy trajectory, or how delay changes with training-set size.
It does not identify a generalizing circuit or memorizing components, or measure Fourier-algorithm formation and removal.
No image, text, or molecule setting, or initialization-scale/weight-norm control of a lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
Weight decay is used in a setup, but the efficiency account, critical dataset size, and ungrokking prediction are not tested.
The study does not identify or compare the algorithms learned across runs.
Numerical measurement recipes are compared for DDS, but the study does not test whether optimizer or softmax numerical artifacts produce or remove the claimed generalization delay.

rows.subject: Nanda modular-addition 1-block transformer
rows.measure: grokking step and fraction of runs grokked
rows.note: The timing does not establish when training accuracy saturated or whether validation accuracy remained at chance before grokking.
rows.check: Setup and selection fact, not a result on the claim. The grok step is defined by val_acc alone (≥0.95 or similar), with no train-accuracy saturation time and no pre-grok chance level. It describes the testbed, not a test.

rows.subject: Barak sparse-parity 2-hidden MLP
rows.measure: grokking step and fraction of runs grokked
rows.note: The timing does not establish when training accuracy saturated or whether validation accuracy remained at chance before grokking.
rows.check: Same as r1: a val_acc-defined grok step only. The stated Barak setup also conflicts internally (30k steps in the setup paragraph vs 240k steps elsewhere).

rows.subject: Nanda modular-addition 1-block transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation-accuracy timing with the dead-direction Fisher observable.
rows.measure: Timing of validation accuracy and u⊤Gu at the dead direction
rows.value: They change synchronously at the grokking transition.
rows.note: This is an accuracy-versus-geometric-observable result, not a training-accuracy-versus-test-accuracy comparison.
rows.check: Compares val_acc with a DDS geometric observable. It does not measure circuit formation or memorization removal, so it cannot bear on V2. The state 'observed' has no version to be observed against.

rows.subject: Barak sparse-parity 2-hidden MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation-accuracy timing with the geometric approach to the singular minimum.
rows.measure: Timing of validation accuracy relative to geometric descent
rows.value: Validation accuracy separates from the geometric approach by thousands of steps; the network learns parity before σmin descends.
rows.note: The reported delay is between validation accuracy and geometric descent, not between training-accuracy saturation and test accuracy.
rows.check: Compares val_acc timing with geometric descent toward a singular minimum, not with train-accuracy saturation or a circuit measure. Locator is better given as Fig. 9(b) / §B.8 than §4.4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Uses grokking transitions as testbeds for spectral measurements rather than testing delayed generalization or the specified circuit mechanisms.

tranche.reason: Uses established grokking benchmarks to evaluate DDS spectral diagnostics against LLC; does not test the stated claim versions.

source_check.notes: The approximately 4× LLC rise and subsequent plateau are explicitly reported for Nanda modular addition (AdamW+CE, 30 seeds), Appendix B.8, lines 2757–2765; Table 2 gives LLC ratios 4.0, 1.02 and 1.05 across the three phases. No rows or verdicts were listed for checking.
